implementation_notes: Catch2 provides the beats as macros: GIVEN/WHEN/THEN map onto SECTIONs and, in the framework's own words, onto the AAA pattern, giving documentation and reporting of those parts without extra comments or code. The classic Testcase Class is replaced by TEST_CASE/SCENARIO plus nested sections, with shared setup factored into a fixture struct or an enclosing section; fall back to TEST_CASE with comments when the BDD vocabulary would overstate what the test abstracts.
pitfalls: Section state is re-created for every leaf path: variables declared in a GIVEN are rebuilt for each WHEN branch, so an expensive arrange belongs in a fixture struct rather than duplicated section bodies.
REQUIRE aborts the current section on failure, so teardown written after the assertion is skipped; use RAII members, or CHECK while diagnosing.
Nothing enforces the sequencing of GIVEN/WHEN/THEN - a WHEN nested inside a THEN compiles and silently reorders the run, as the Catch2 docs warn.

variants.name: GoogleTest TEST_F fixture (SetUp as the arrange beat)
variants.idiom_name: GoogleTest TEST_F with a testing::Test fixture class
variants.implementation_notes: The classic xUnit shape: derive a fixture from testing::Test, prepare the arrange beat in SetUp() or the constructor, then keep one act and its assertions in each TEST_F body with TearDown() for cleanup; GoogleTest creates a fresh fixture per test, so tests stay independent. ASSERT_* aborts the test body while EXPECT_* records the failure and continues, so prefer EXPECT_* in the assert beat unless the rest of the test depends on the value.
pitfalls: SetUp() misspelled as Setup() is not an override and the arrange beat silently never runs - the primer calls this out and recommends marking it override.
A fatal ASSERT_* returns from the test body at once, skipping hand-written cleanup after it; prefer EXPECT_* in the assert beat or RAII members for the teardown.
